ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
An open electrical circuit contains a wire loop in the shape of a semi-circle, that contains a resistor of resistance $R=0.2 \Omega$. The circuit is completed by a conducting pendulum in the form of a uniform rod with length $\ell=0.1 \mathrm{~m}$ and mass $m=0.05 \mathrm{~kg}$, has no resistance, and stays in contact with the other wires at all times. All electrical components are oriented in the $y z$ plane, and gravity acts in the $z$ direction. A constant magnetic field of strength $B=2 \mathrm{~T}$ is applied in the $+x$ direction.
<image_1>

Ignoring self inductance and assuming that $\alpha \ll 1$, the general equation of motion is in the form of $\theta(t)=A(t) \cos (\omega t+\varphi)$, where $A(t) \geq 0$. Find $\omega^{2}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The circuit in the figure lies in the yz plane within the plane of the paper, and is a semicircular guide rail; a resistor R is connected in series in the fixed wire above. The length of the uniform conducting rod is labeled ℓ; one end is near the upper contact point, and the other end is in contact with the semicircular guide rail. The small angular displacement between the rod and the dashed vertical equilibrium position is labeled α. Many dotted circles in the figure indicate that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the paper outward, namely along the +x direction; the arrow on the right indicates gravity g downward. Reasoning: When the rod rotates, the area of the closed loop changes with angle. From the sector area swept out by the rod in the figure, dA/dθ = ℓ^2/2, so the induced electromotive force ε = B(ℓ^2/2) θdot. The current I = ε/R = Bℓ^2 θdot/(2R). The electromagnetic damping power equals Joule heat: P = I^2 R = B^2ℓ^4 θdot^2/(4R). Therefore the damping torque satisfies τ_mag θdot = -P, giving τ_mag = -[B^2ℓ^4/(4R)] θdot. The moment of inertia of a uniform rod rotating about an endpoint is I_rot = mℓ^2/3; the small-angle gravitational restoring torque is τ_g = -mgℓ θ/2. Thus the equation of motion is (mℓ^2/3) θddot + [B^2ℓ^4/(4R)] θdot + (mgℓ/2) θ = 0. The standard damped oscillator form is θddot + 2β θdot + ω0^2 θ = 0, where ω0^2 = 3g/(2ℓ), 2β = [B^2ℓ^4/(4R)]/(mℓ^2/3). Substitute numerical values: ω0^2 = 3(9.8)/(2×0.1) = 147; the damping coefficient term c/I_rot = [2^2(0.1)^4/(4×0.2)]/[0.05(0.1)^2/3] = 3, so β = 1.5. Therefore the square of the actual oscillation angular frequency is ω^2 = ω0^2 - β^2 = 147 - 2.25 = 144.75 ≈ 145.

raw_record.question_text:
An open electrical circuit contains a wire loop in the shape of a semi-circle, that contains a resistor of resistance $R=0.2 \Omega$. The circuit is completed by a conducting pendulum in the form of a uniform rod with length $\ell=0.1 \mathrm{~m}$ and mass $m=0.05 \mathrm{~kg}$, has no resistance, and stays in contact with the other wires at all times. All electrical components are oriented in the $y z$ plane, and gravity acts in the $z$ direction. A constant magnetic field of strength $B=2 \mathrm{~T}$ is applied in the $+x$ direction.

Ignoring self inductance and assuming that $\alpha \ll 1$, the general equation of motion is in the form of $\theta(t)=A(t) \cos (\omega t+\varphi)$, where $A(t) \geq 0$. Find $\omega^{2}$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the rod is a conducting pendulum of length ℓ pivoted at the upper dot, its lower end sliding on a semicircular rail centered at the pivot; the dashed vertical line marks the equilibrium position, and α/θ is the small angular displacement. The resistor is in the fixed upper part of the circuit, and the dotted circles show the magnetic field perpendicular to the yz plane. From the text, use R = 0.2 Ω, ℓ = 0.1 m, m = 0.05 kg, B = 2 T, no self-inductance, and small-angle motion. Use the changing magnetic flux through the sector swept by the rod: dA/dθ = ℓ²/2, so the induced emf is ε = B(ℓ²/2)θdot and current I = ε/R. The magnetic damping can be found from Joule loss, P = I²R = τ_mag θdot, giving τ_mag = -[B²ℓ⁴/(4R)]θdot. Combine this with the small-angle physical-pendulum torque for a uniform rod, I_rot = mℓ²/3 and τ_g = -mgℓθ/2, to get I_rot θddot + [B²ℓ⁴/(4R)]θdot + mgℓθ/2 = 0. Identify the damped oscillation frequency from θddot + 2βθdot + ω0²θ = 0, where ω0² = 3g/(2ℓ) and β = [B²ℓ⁴/(4R)]/[2mℓ²/3]. Then compute ω² = ω0² - β² ≈ 145.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the rod rotates in the yz plane about its upper contact while its lower end slides along the semicircular wire; the magnetic field dots indicate a field normal to the circuit plane, and gravity points downward along the dashed equilibrium direction. From the text, take R = 0.2 Ω, ℓ = 0.1 m, m = 0.05 kg, B = 2 T, with the rod resistance negligible. Instead of using flux, compute the motional emf directly along the moving rod. A rod element at distance s from the pivot has speed v = sθdot, so the local motional field along the rod has magnitude B sθdot. Integrating along the rod gives ε = ∫0^ℓ B sθdot ds = Bℓ²θdot/2, hence current I = Bℓ²θdot/(2R). Then calculate the magnetic torque directly: each element experiences dF = I B ds perpendicular to the rod, so dτ = s I B ds, and τ_mag = -∫0^ℓ s I B ds = -B²ℓ⁴θdot/(4R). Add the gravitational restoring torque of the uniform rod, -mgℓθ/2, and use I_rot = mℓ²/3. The resulting linear equation is θddot + [B²ℓ⁴/(4R I_rot)]θdot + [mgℓ/(2I_rot)]θ = 0. Reading off the underdamped frequency gives ω² = 3g/(2ℓ) - {B²ℓ⁴/[8R I_rot]}², which evaluates to about 145.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中电路位于纸面内的 yz 平面。外侧导线是半圆形轨道，上方有一个标注为 R 的电阻；一根长度标为 ℓ 的导体杆连接上方接触点和半圆轨道上的下方接触点，杆相对竖直虚线偏转小角 α。图中许多带点圆圈表示磁场垂直纸面向外，即沿 +x 方向；右侧箭头标出重力 g 向下。导体杆始终与上端导线和下端半圆导线接触，构成闭合回路。

推理：按指定方法，直接计算运动杆上的动生电动势。杆上距转轴 s 的微元速度大小为 v=s θdot，磁场 B 垂直于运动平面，因此沿杆方向的动生电场大小为 B s θdot。积分得 ε=∫_0^ℓ B s θdot ds=Bℓ²θdot/2。由于只有电阻 R 起作用，电流 I=ε/R=Bℓ²θdot/(2R)。

磁力对杆产生阻尼力矩。每段长度 ds 受磁力 dF=I B ds，其对转轴的力矩微元 dτ=s I B ds，方向反抗运动，所以 τ_mag=-∫_0^ℓ s I B ds=-I B ℓ²/2=-B²ℓ⁴θdot/(4R)。

均匀杆绕上端转动的转动惯量 I_rot=mℓ²/3。小角度下重力恢复力矩为 τ_g=-(mgℓ/2)θ。因此线性方程为 I_rot θddot + B²ℓ⁴/(4R) θdot + mgℓ/2 θ=0，即 θddot + [B²ℓ⁴/(4R I_rot)]θdot + [mgℓ/(2I_rot)]θ=0。

这是阻尼振子，若写成 θ(t)=A(t)cos(ωt+φ)，则 ω²=mgℓ/(2I_rot)-[B²ℓ⁴/(8R I_rot)]²。代入 I_rot=mℓ²/3，得第一项 mgℓ/(2I_rot)=3g/(2ℓ)。数值上 I_rot=0.05×0.1²/3=1.6667×10^-4 kg·m²；3g/(2ℓ)=3×9.8/(0.2)=147；B²ℓ⁴/(8R I_rot)=2²×0.1⁴/(8×0.2×1.6667×10^-4)=1.5。因此 ω²=147-1.5²=144.75≈145。

图像描述：图中电路位于纸面内的 yz 平面。外侧导线是半圆形轨道，上方有一个标注为 R 的电阻；一根长度标为 ℓ 的导体杆连接上方接触点和半圆轨道上的下方接触点，杆相对竖直虚线偏转小角 α。图中许多带点圆圈表示磁场垂直纸面向外，即沿 +x 方向；右侧箭头标出重力 g 向下。导体杆始终与上端导线和下端半圆导线接触，构成闭合回路。

推理：按指定方法，直接计算运动杆上的动生电动势。杆上距转轴 s 的微元速度大小为 v=s θdot，磁场 B 垂直于运动平面，因此沿杆方向的动生电场大小为 B s θdot。积分得 ε=∫_0^ℓ B s θdot ds=Bℓ²θdot/2。由于只有电阻 R 起作用，电流 I=ε/R=Bℓ²θdot/(2R)。

磁力对杆产生阻尼力矩。每段长度 ds 受磁力 dF=I B ds，其对转轴的力矩微元 dτ=s I B ds，方向反抗运动，所以 τ_mag=-∫_0^ℓ s I B ds=-I B ℓ²/2=-B²ℓ⁴θdot/(4R)。

均匀杆绕上端转动的转动惯量 I_rot=mℓ²/3。小角度下重力恢复力矩为 τ_g=-(mgℓ/2)θ。因此线性方程为 I_rot θddot + B²ℓ⁴/(4R) θdot + mgℓ/2 θ=0，即 θddot + [B²ℓ⁴/(4R I_rot)]θdot + [mgℓ/(2I_rot)]θ=0。

这是阻尼振子，若写成 θ(t)=A(t)cos(ωt+φ)，则 ω²=mgℓ/(2I_rot)-[B²ℓ⁴/(8R I_rot)]²。代入 I_rot=mℓ²/3，得第一项 mgℓ/(2I_rot)=3g/(2ℓ)。数值上 I_rot=0.05×0.1²/3=1.6667×10^-4 kg·m²；3g/(2ℓ)=3×9.8/(0.2)=147；B²ℓ⁴/(8R I_rot)=2²×0.1⁴/(8×0.2×1.6667×10^-4)=1.5。因此 ω²=147-1.5²=144.75≈145。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This route derives both the induced current and magnetic damping torque locally from motional emf and Lorentz force, rather than from global flux and power balance.
planner_metadata.image_role: Use the image to see that only the straight rod is moving, that a point on it has speed proportional to distance from the pivot, and that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of rotation.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the given circuit resistance, rod length and mass, magnetic field strength, no self-inductance condition, and small-angle approximation.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply motional emf integration, magnetic force on a current-carrying wire, torque integration about a pivot, uniform-rod rotational inertia, small-angle gravity torque, and the damped oscillator frequency relation.

raw_record.original_question:
An open electrical circuit contains a wire loop in the shape of a semi-circle, that contains a resistor of resistance $R=0.2 \Omega$. The circuit is completed by a conducting pendulum in the form of a uniform rod with length $\ell=0.1 \mathrm{~m}$ and mass $m=0.05 \mathrm{~kg}$, has no resistance, and stays in contact with the other wires at all times. All electrical components are oriented in the $y z$ plane, and gravity acts in the $z$ direction. A constant magnetic field of strength $B=2 \mathrm{~T}$ is applied in the $+x$ direction.

Ignoring self inductance and assuming that $\alpha \ll 1$, the general equation of motion is in the form of $\theta(t)=A(t) \cos (\omega t+\varphi)$, where $A(t) \geq 0$. Find $\omega^{2}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The circuit in the figure lies in the yz plane within the plane of the paper, and is a semicircular guide rail; a resistor R is connected in series in the fixed wire above. The length of the uniform conducting rod is labeled ℓ; one end is near the upper contact point, and the other end is in contact with the semicircular guide rail. The small angular displacement between the rod and the dashed vertical equilibrium position is labeled α. Many dotted circles in the figure indicate that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the paper outward, namely along the +x direction; the arrow on the right indicates gravity g downward.

Reasoning: When the rod rotates, the area of the closed loop changes with angle. From the sector area swept out by the rod in the figure, dA/dθ = ℓ^2/2, so the induced electromotive force ε = B(ℓ^2/2) θdot. The current I = ε/R = Bℓ^2 θdot/(2R). The electromagnetic damping power equals Joule heat: P = I^2 R = B^2ℓ^4 θdot^2/(4R). Therefore the damping torque satisfies τ_mag θdot = -P, giving τ_mag = -[B^2ℓ^4/(4R)] θdot. The moment of inertia of a uniform rod rotating about an endpoint is I_rot = mℓ^2/3; the small-angle gravitational restoring torque is τ_g = -mgℓ θ/2. Thus the equation of motion is (mℓ^2/3) θddot + [B^2ℓ^4/(4R)] θdot + (mgℓ/2) θ = 0. The standard damped oscillator form is θddot + 2β θdot + ω0^2 θ = 0, where ω0^2 = 3g/(2ℓ), 2β = [B^2ℓ^4/(4R)]/(mℓ^2/3). Substitute numerical values: ω0^2 = 3(9.8)/(2×0.1) = 147; the damping coefficient term c/I_rot = [2^2(0.1)^4/(4×0.2)]/[0.05(0.1)^2/3] = 3, so β = 1.5. Therefore the square of the actual oscillation angular frequency is ω^2 = ω0^2 - β^2 = 147 - 2.25 = 144.75 ≈ 145.

No revision is necessary.
